method: For each pre-registered query the seeked `view` reports its ObservationStats (including the instrumented bytes_read from the reader's CountingReader) and wall/CPU/peak-RSS from /usr/bin/time -v; every served slice is byte-compared (cmp) against the source. The same query is re-run under `strace -f -e trace=read,pread64 -P <descriptor>` so the bytes returned and the read-call count are attributed to the descriptor file alone (no loader, no pipe). Each sequential baseline is timed directly with /usr/bin/time -v while a FIFO-fed consumer closes after the target output offset; gzip/zstd/xz decompress the same prefix (a+len bytes) and `pv -b -n` counts the compressed bytes read. CPU time is user+sys.
caveats: The descriptor's instrumented bytes_read is the primary metric; the strace figure equals it + 64 B (the CLI header peek). OS page cache dominates wall time, not read() byte counts. The sequential decoders' compressed-prefix figures are measured at a pipe and so include a bounded read-ahead: they are close upper bounds, not exact seek figures. Single locally generated corpus; no population claim.
